messages:
jane.cook: FYI - rolled the RBAC schema refactor back in staging but seeing weird role affinity where some sessions still get the new-role permissions :thinking: 
arjun.k: ugh, details? which service? any 403s?
sarah.m: saw 403 from billing-worker in staging for user 7642, looks like their role_id still points to the new seeded role after rollback. logs attached. :eyes:
leo: can you paste the backfill query you ran? might have updated role_map rather than role_assignment table by mistake.
jane.cook: backfill script: ```sql
UPDATE role_assignments ra
SET role_id = r.new_role_id
FROM role_seed_map r
WHERE ra.legacy_role_code = r.legacy_code
  AND ra.role_id != r.new_role_id;
```
jane.cook: we ran that as a one-off during canary then rolled back the migration code but forgot to reverse the backfill.
arjun.k: that explains sticky affinity — data change persisted. do we have audit events for the UPDATE? check audit_log for actor = 'migration-service'.
jane.cook: checking... partial audit rows present but a chunk is missing for timespan 12:34-12:40. some entries show `kms: decrypt failed` while trying to unwrap service token. snippet: ```ERROR kms: access denied for key projects/redwood-keys/locations/global/keyRings/default/cryptoKeys/rbac-migration-key: PermissionDenied```
eva: ohhh KMS failure, that would abort some writes and leave the db half-updated?
sarah.m: if the migration service couldn't decrypt creds for a subset of workers, they'd skip writes. we likely have a window of mixed state.
leo: need quick inventory: 1) find all role_assignments modified by migration 2) reconcile with intended seed map 3) run compensating update to restore old roles for rollback path.
arjun.k: agree. also important: generate an immutable audit snapshot before applying compensating updates. we must not hide what happened for compliance.
jane.cook: got a query to list affected rows: ```sql
SELECT ra.id, ra.user_id, ra.role_id, ra.updated_at FROM role_assignments ra
JOIN role_seed_audit rsa ON rsa.legacy_code = ra.legacy_code
WHERE ra.updated_at BETWEEN '2026-03-18T12:00:00Z' AND '2026-03-18T13:00:00Z';
```
jane.cook: running now, 142 rows returned.
eva: can we map those role_ids back to previous values? do we have a pre-backfill snapshot or binlog?
sarah.m: wal-archive has entries, but we'll need to replay to get old role_id per row. fallback: look at auth_events table for last assignment per user before 12:00.
leo: for safety: create a compensating update plan staged as a transaction script with logging to `compensating_updates` table + dry-run first.
arjun.k: add a check to ensure KMS keys are present and accessible for all worker zones before applying. if KMS fails again we'll corrupt more state.
infra-bot: Deploy 1895012320: rbac-migration-service -> rolled back by deploy-bot at 2026-03-18T12:45Z.
jane.cook: thanks infra-bot. question: was the migration using envelope keys with customer KMS? it's our default keyRings. if access was intermittent maybe a transient permission expiry on the migration service SA.
eva: looked at IAM logs, there was a short-lived deny for service-account:migration@redwood.iam at 12:33 due to a temporary policy sync. cloud-admin is already aware. 
arjun.k: ok but action items: (A) produce list of affected users and intended previous roles (B) generate compensating txns with audit logging (C) run audit export to S3 and snapshot before changes (D) coordinate with cloud-admin to ensure KMS stable and send a page to oncall if not.
sarah.m: I'll take A and C. ETA 30m.
leo: I'll draft compensating script and dry-run it on staging. include `WHERE id IN (...)` explicit set to avoid wide updates.
jane.cook: include an instrumentation flag: `--record-reconciliation=true` to write each change to `compensating_updates` with before/after and operator id.
arjun.k: good. also update the rollout checklist: add post-backfill verification step to compare role counts and sample auth flows.
eva: tagging @cloud-admin in ticket now.
leo: small note — any tokens issued during the mixed window may have cached claims. we should expire session tokens for affected users. code to revoke: ```bash
python tools/revoke_sessions.py --user-ids $(cat affected_users.txt) --reason "RBAC rollback reconciliation"
```
jane.cook: agree, include token expiry in plan.
deploy-bot: Incident note created: INC-20260318-06 - RBAC backfill partial failure due to KMS transient deny.
arjun.k: after reconciliation we'll run an eval set of 50 user flows to ensure no privilege escalation. if anything looks off, pause and escalate.
sarah.m: uploading audit export to gs://redwood-compliance/rb ackups/1895012345-audit-snapshot.json.gz - link: https://storage.googleapis.com/redwood-compliance/...
jane.cook: thanks. I'll coordinate the recon later today and post a short postmortem draft. :+1:
leo: status update: dry-run shows 142 candidate compensating updates, no FK issues. scheduling real run at 13:30 UTC behind maintenance flag.
ev a: once done please update the compliance ticket with checksums of pre/post exports. auditors will need that.
arjun.k: final reminder: add a guard in migration service to abort on any KMS decrypt errors and surface as a hard fail, not partial skip. we also need automated alerting when audit rows count mismatches expected.
jane.cook: noted. will submit PR for both.
infra-bot: Runbook step logged: rbk-rollback-20260318 by jane.cook at 2026-03-18T13:05Z.
sarah.m: closing loop here after run. will post results.
jane.cook: thanks team.
